answer: The NASA records do not contain enough charging samples at 3.5-4.62 A and 80-90% SOC (n = 0, 0, 1, 2 for RW9-RW12) to test whether RW11 stays below 4.20 V in that regime, so that comparison is insufficient. Where the high-current data are sufficient (3.5-4.62 A x 50-60% SOC), RW11 measured median voltage is 4.228 V (n=128), which is not below RW9 (4.198 V, n=111); RW11 also has the most charging samples with I_chg > 4 A and V >= 4.1 V (44859). The RW11 cell twin under-predicts voltage in that sufficient high-current bin (bias -0.03252301773428922 V), more than twin_source_RW9.pt on the same RW11 windows (bias -0.009617232143878988 V). RW11 extra current headroom in GP-BO is a twin (especially fine-tune) effect, not a pattern the measured high-current voltages support.
